meaning.evidence: "from sunup till 2 p.m. each day" preserves the earlier partial opening, distinct from the September all-day opening; the temperatures, warnings and handling guidance all survive.

sense.evidence: "knock fish off" correctly means kill here, and "Don't play hooked trout till they're stuffed" preserves the angling sense of play and the exhaustion warning.

authenticity.evidence: "quick smart" and "come good" fit ordinary Australian usage, but the accumulated "yer", "ya" and dropped endings make the presentation slightly performed.

register.evidence: "Anglers'll be right" and "Pitchin' in like this'll" sustain the strong conversational register asked for, within the vulgarity allowance.

tone.evidence: "Handle fish gently and keep 'em in the water" maintains the serious conservation advice beneath the relaxed voice.

flow.evidence: "These rivers were shut to fishin' altogether from July 15, then that got wound back" carries the chronology smoothly despite the dense opening list.

variety.evidence: "wound back", "keep an eye on", "quick smart", "stuffed" and "come good" give varied phrasing without an intrusive repeated catchphrase.

essence.evidence: "Update: Yellowstone lifts full closures on Firehole, Madison and Gibbon rivers" retains the layered update format, operational notice and fish-protection purpose.

problems.why: The extensive phonetic spellings, represented by ya alongside yer and many dropped endings, give otherwise idiomatic speech a slightly performed surface.

A.summary: Complete and clear conservation advice in a convincing full-yarn register, with slightly conspicuous eye dialect.

meaning.evidence: "the remaining fishing restrictions" and "Partial restrictions stay in place from 2 p.m. to sunrise the next day" retain the two dated stages accurately, including locations and conditions.

sense.evidence: "Don't wear hooked trout out by playing them to exhaustion" correctly disambiguates the angling term and preserves the warning.

authenticity.evidence: "Doing your bit" and "cos water flows were low" are natural informal Australian phrasing with no forced slang.

register.evidence: "Anglers will be able to fish these rivers" and "temporary restrictions may be lifted" remain essentially neutral notice prose; the very light colloquial touch misses level 5.

tone.evidence: "Handle fish gently" and "It may also avoid the need to ban fishing" keep the original's cooperative, protective intent.

flow.evidence: "depending on how conditions shape up when assessed" has an awkward redundant ending, repeated later; the rest reads smoothly.

variety.evidence: "Doing your bit", "stay in place" and "cooling down" vary the wording without relying on stock tags.

essence.evidence: "as set out in the 2026 Fishing Regulations booklet" and both updates preserve the regulatory purpose and practical character.

problems.quote: Anglers will be able to fish these rivers
problems.original: Anglers will be able to fish these rivers
problems.why: The largely unchanged formal register is far lighter than the full pub yarn requested.

problems.quote: how conditions shape up when assessed
problems.why: Shape up when assessed is an awkward combination, and it recurs in the second monitoring notice.

B.summary: Faithful and appropriately careful, but far too restrained for level 5 and occasionally awkward in the monitoring language.

meaning.evidence: "Part-day restrictions still on from 2 p.m. to sunup the next day" and "over 68 degrees Fahrenheit (20 degrees Celsius)" retain the timing, threshold and fish-safety rationale alongside the full notice.

sense.evidence: "Don't play a hooked trout till it's knackered" preserves the technical sense of playing a fish and its exhaustion; "come good" fits recovery.

authenticity.evidence: "Good news for fishos" and "Do us a favour" create a credible Australian oral voice, with a slight performed edge from pervasive "ya" and "yer" spellings.

register.evidence: "fishos can have a go" and "save 'em havin' to ban fishin'" make a sustained strong vernacular retelling within the allowed vulgarity.

tone.evidence: "If everyone does the right thing, it'll look after the park's fisheries" preserves the cooperative conservation appeal rather than making light of fish deaths.

flow.evidence: "Staff'll keep an eye on the water temperatures, mind" is an easy spoken pivot, and the chronological updates remain clear aloud.

variety.evidence: "fishos", "wound back", "mind", "knackered" and "come good" provide a varied vocabulary while the necessary repeated restrictions stay recognisable.

essence.evidence: "like it says in the 2026 Fishing Regulations booklet" keeps the regulatory anchor and the two-stage update structure remains unmistakable.

problems.why: Persistent phonetic spellings make the otherwise plausible spoken voice slightly self-conscious on the page.

C.summary: A clear and faithful full yarn that preserves practical urgency and cooperation; comparable overall to A.
